Note::nlp¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

NoteNlpAccessor Note::nlp() const noexcept

Enter The Linguistic Operation Surface¶

nlp() binds a lightweight accessor to the current Note. The accessor groups linguistic analysis, corpus cleanup, token extraction, phonetic transforms, and language-oriented comparison without crowding the general Note surface with prefixed method names.

The call does not analyze text, allocate storage, copy the Note, or change its dtype. It returns a temporary proxy containing one pointer to the receiver; the selected operation performs the work. This keeps Note itself a one-pointer intrusive handle while allowing fluent pipelines:

const auto cleaned = text.nlp().remove_html();
const auto words = cleaned.nlp().tokens();

The accessor is valid for the full expression in which it is created. Store the Note, not the accessor, when work must outlive that expression. Each accessor method documents its own accepted dtype, shape behavior, options, and result type.

Open the Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Example: Cleanup Then Tokenization¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({"<b>Ship</b> #release today"});
const auto plain = source.nlp().remove_html().nlp().remove_hashtags();
const auto words = plain.nlp().tokens();

std::cout << pluss::note::print(plain) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(words.tokens()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Ship today"]
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["Ship", "today"]

The first call strips element syntax but keeps Ship; the second removes the tag token, and tokens() then represents the two remaining words as the Text member of a closed TokenBatch. Use words.tokens() for the flat values and words.offsets() for the cumulative row boundaries; neither is a root Note method.
